findings: The route documents Link in the Web Elements Payment Request Button, with existence of a supported pre-Endive Stripe.js version a prerequisite for the legacy behavior. A customer new to the merchant site can already have saved Link details. A returning Link customer clicks Link and enters an SMS or email code to load details and enable one-click payment. An account authenticated on this or another Link-enabled business in the prior 90 days can skip reauthentication. A customer new to Link is prompted to save details upon clicking. Old raw 10–19 and new 15–24. These are UI and Link-account authentication/enrollment states, not server-side payment completion.

Old raw 12 and new 17 preserve the route's documented compatibility with card features such as subscriptions, no additional Link fees, and turning it on/off through payment method settings. Scope these claims to the supported legacy route; they do not specify all subscription scenarios, merchant pricing, or status/settlement outcomes. Source 19–23 preserves the window, fees and enrollment but leaves out the normal returning SMS/email authentication and saved-detail loading.

On supported PRB versions, Connect auto-availability is for connected accounts accessing the Element through their platform integration. The platform manages settings for platform-processed payments, and a connected account manages its own via its Dashboard for payments processed without a platform. Old raw 21–26 and new 26–31; current source 25–29 preserves the management split. The route does not equate the settings split with a particular Connect charge type or imply support on Endive.

The 2026-09-30 changelog captured 2026-11-07 specifies that elements.create('paymentRequestButton') throws from Endive and integrations using React PaymentRequestButtonElement are affected. Stripe.js through Dahlia continues to support the Element, subject to the parent raw route's supported-version qualification (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-deprecate-payment-request-button-2026-11-07.md:5–17). These are Stripe.js Web Elements limits, separate from the server API version and separate retained package-declaration evidence in wiki/concepts/stripe-express-checkout-element.md:217–225.
substantive_changes: May says Stripe no longer recommends PRB for Web Elements and lists Link Authentication Element, Express Checkout Element and Payment Element (old raw 8). November explicitly deprecates the PRB integration, establishes unsupported Stripe.js Endive and later versus supported earlier versions, recommends migration to Express Checkout Element, and names Contact Details Element or Payment Element as other Link paths (new raw 9–13). This adds an explicit compatibility boundary and revised migration guidance.

The Contact Details name in new raw 13 is material migration guidance. The separate Contact Details Link guide at raw/stripe-payments-link-contact-details-element-2026-11-07.md:5–20 calls it previously known as Link Authentication Element and uses it for email collection and Link auth before Payment Element. Its example at 24–49 uses elements.create('contactDetails', ...). This supports a product/documentation rename and distinct integration, with no alias compatibility or PRB behavior transfer established.

The migration link targets a separately scoped guide. Its November capture is a variant index for Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents (raw/stripe-elements-express-checkout-element-migration-2026-11-07.md:5–14), while the full 2026-04-21 Payment Intents guide requires legacy Charges API with tokens integrations first to migrate to Payment Intents (raw/stripe-express-checkout-element-migration-2025.md:4–13). The link itself and unchanged See also entries are navigation. The image path/alt-text and heading whitespace are presentational.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-link-payment-request-button-link-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-payment-request-button-link-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-request-button-link.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-request-button-link`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-request-button-link, old raw lines 4-12 only advised against the legacy Payment Request Button route. New raw lines 5-17 explicitly mark it deprecated and unsupported in Stripe.js Endive or later. It continues to work in earlier Stripe.js versions only as long as those versions are supported. November recommends migration to Express Checkout Element or using another preferred Element such as Contact Details or Payment Element. On the supported legacy browser route, a person new to the merchant can already have a Link account and pay with saved details. Returning Link customers click Link and authenticate with an SMS or email code, then Link loads their saved payment details. Prior authentication within 90 days at this or another Link-enabled business can skip reauthentication. A customer new to Link is prompted to save details. Both old raw lines 10-19 and new raw lines 15-24 retain payment method settings, compatibility with card features including subscriptions and no additional Link fees. Both old raw lines 21-26 and new raw lines 26-31 say connected accounts accessing the Element via a platform get Link automatically, the platform manages the settings for payments processed through it, and the connected account manages the setting for independent payments via its own Dashboard. source-stripe-payment-request-button-link.md lines 13-29 preserve the 90-day and Connect details but lack the explicit cutoff, revised alternatives and normal returning SMS/email flow. Authentication, loaded payment credentials and the ability to make a one-click payment do not show that a payment succeeded.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-request-button-link, old raw lines 4-12 and new raw lines 5-17 show the substantive integration change in the captured guidance: the May no-longer-recommended Web Elements path and its Link Authentication, Express Checkout and Payment Element alternatives become an explicit Stripe.js Endive-and-later support cutoff in November, earlier supported Stripe.js versions retain the Element, and the guide directs migration to Express Checkout or another preferred Element such as Contact Details or Payment Element. The 2026-09-30 Endive changelog, captured November 7, confirms that elements.create('paymentRequestButton') throws starting with Endive, React PaymentRequestButtonElement integrations are affected, and Stripe.js through Dahlia retains the Element (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-deprecate-payment-request-button-2026-11-07.md lines 5-17). Keep the May 8, 2026 wording and legacy provenance dated in source-stripe-payment-request-button-link.md lines 13-17 and in the reciprocal Link concept section. The separate Contact Details guide identifies the former Link Authentication name and a distinct checkout/email flow. Add reciprocal compatibility context to the Express Checkout migration route, whose November capture is only Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents navigation. The separately captured April full Payment Intents migration requires Charges API with tokens integrations to migrate to Payment Intents first. The old and new See also links are navigation and the CDN/alt-text/whitespace edits are presentational. Old raw lines 17-26 and new raw lines 22-31 retain the authentication and Connect behavior conditionally for the supported legacy client Element. The cutoff does not imply removal of stripe.paymentRequest() or a server API change. Neither the authentication window, subscription claim nor the settings split proves a successful charge, authorization, settlement or actual merchant/connected-account eligibility.
